newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rallies late as dollar slides abroad.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rallies late as dollar slides abroad.

text.p: Selling pressure on the Thai baht eased significantly in late trade on Friday helped by the dollar's sharp decline against major currencies abroad, dealers said.
The baht was trading higher at 25.995/26.005 to the dollar late from 26.017/26.022 early, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.99 per dollar against 26.05 on Thursday.
"Selling pressure on the baht had calmed down significantly in the afternoon. Players were reluctant to take further long dollar positions," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

The baht faced some panic selling today, precipitated by rumours that Thai authorities might be holding a meeting on the currency which could lead to a widening of the dollar/baht band, market sources said.
The Bank of Thailand on Friday denied the rumour, saying the present trading band and exchange rate mechanisms will not be changed.
The central bank's intervention to sell dollars in Singapore also weakened selling interest of the baht for the dollar, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate fell to 9.00 percent in late trade from 9.50-9.75 in the morning on rising liquidity, dealers said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 6.00/6.50 satangs per dollar late compared with 6.00/7.00 in early trade, dealers said.
